text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

Abstract
This report answers whether the GEO accessions GSE309890 and GDS309890 refer to the same record. I queried NCBI GEO accession resolution using the geo_resolve_accession tool with the two accessions as input. The call requested two accessions and resolved both (2 requested, 2 resolved). The response returned distinct metadata for each accession: GSE309890 (UID 200309890, entry_type "GSE") and GDS309890 (UID 309890, entry_type "GDS"), each with separate FTP directory and GEO query URLs. Based on the returned entry_type and UID values, the two accessions are different GEO record classes and are not the same record. This matters because researchers who confuse GSE and GDS accessions may retrieve the wrong dataset or metadata; resolving accession types prevents misinterpretation. The provenance for the metadata URLs is provided so readers can inspect the two records directly.

I. Introduction
Background. The question concerns two NCBI GEO accessions: GSE309890 and GDS309890. GEO accessions encode record identity and type; distinguishing accession classes is necessary to retrieve the intended data and metadata.

Literature Review. The only records retrieved for this query are the geo_resolve_accession response entries for:
- GSE309890 (geo URL and FTP directory) and
- GDS309890 (geo URL and FTP directory).
No other literature or external PubMed records were retrieved for this query.

Knowledge Gap. It was unresolved in the query whether the two accession strings denote the same GEO record or different GEO records/classes.

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine if GSE309890 and GDS309890 are the same GEO record. Hypothesis: they are different records because the accession prefixes (GSE vs GDS) represent different GEO entry types; therefore the two accession identifiers will resolve to distinct metadata entries.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. A targeted accession-resolution lookup was chosen because the question asks about equivalence of accession identifiers; resolving accessions to their GEO metadata directly answers whether they map to the same record.

Materials. I used the geo_resolve_accession function (an NCBI GEO accession-resolution utility exposed by the geo_resolve_accession tool).

Procedures. Tool call (single step), exact arguments:
- Function invoked: geo_resolve_accession
- Parameter: accessions = "GSE309890 GDS309890"
- No additional filters or arguments were passed.

The tool returned a JSON object containing:
- requested: number of accessions supplied (2)
- resolved: number of accessions resolved (2)
- results: an array of per-accession resolution records with fields uid, accession, entry_type, ftp_directory_url, geo_url
- rule: "UID = type digit + accession number padded to 8 digits. GPL=1, GSE=2, GSM=3, and GDS takes no digit at all."

Statistical Analysis. Counts and proportions derive directly from the tool response:
- Denominator for resolution rate = requested (2). Numerator = resolved (2). Resolution proportion = 2/2 = 100%.
- Per-accession fields (uid, entry_type, ftp_directory_url, geo_url) were taken directly from the result rows without modification or deduplication. No further statistical tests were applied.

III. Results
Data Presentation.

Table 1. Resolved accession metadata returned by geo_resolve_accession.
| accession | uid      | entry_type | ftp_directory_url                                                                     | geo_url                                                                   |
|-----------|----------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890 | 200309890| GSE        | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/                          | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890              |
| GDS309890 | 309890   | GDS        | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/                        | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890              |

Findings.
- Number of accessions requested: 2.
- Number of accessions resolved: 2 (resolution rate 100%).
- The two accessions resolved to distinct records: GSE309890 has entry_type "GSE" and uid 200309890; GDS309890 has entry_type "GDS" and uid 309890.
- Each accession has a separate FTP directory URL and separate GEO query URL as shown in Table 1.
- The tool-provided rule indicates distinct UID encoding for different GEO types (GPL=1, GSE=2, GSM=3; GDS handled without a digit), consistent with differing entry_type values.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The query results show that GSE309890 and GDS309890 are different GEO records: they have different entry_type values, different UIDs, and different FTP and GEO URLs. Therefore, GSE309890 is not the same thing as GDS309890.

Context. The finding directly follows from the geo_resolve_accession output: two requested accessions resolved to two distinct resolution records. The "entry_type" field is the immediate indicator that the accession prefixes correspond to different GEO record classes.

Limitations. The geo_resolve_accession response provides metadata-level resolution (uids, entry_type, ftp_directory_url, geo_url) but does not return the full record contents, record descriptions, or the biological data within each accession. This analysis cannot state how the contents of the two records relate (for example, whether one is derived from or summarizes the other) without fetching the full GEO entries themselves. Also, the tool response explains UID rule structure but does not provide formal definitions of the GEO entry_type labels beyond the values returned.

Conclusion & Future Directions. Conclusion: GSE309890 and GDS309890 are distinct GEO accessions and not the same record. A useful next query is to fetch the full GEO entries using the provided geo_url links (or use the geo_series call for GSE and an appropriate GEO record fetch for GDS) to inspect titles, summaries, and content to understand how (if at all) the datasets relate.

References
[1] NCBI GEO (geo_resolve_accession result for GSE309890), ftp_directory_url: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[2] NCBI GEO (geo_resolve_accession result for GSE309890), geo_url: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[3] NCBI GEO (geo_resolve_accession result for GDS309890), ftp_directory_url: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/
[4] NCBI GEO (geo_resolve_accession result for GDS309890), geo_url: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890

Data provided by NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) via the geo_resolve_accession tool.
